title: Bridge black-box gaps between console ingress and runtime via eBPF-derived metrics and deterministic sampled-span policy
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: During the 2026-03-02 capacity/regression incident we lost effective lineage between Console ingress events and downstream runtime processing for ~14 minutes. The primary blind spots were: (1) no network-level per-tenant ingress counters on edge nodes (we only had aggregated LB metrics), and (2) traced spans were sampled probabilistically in a way that systematically dropped spans crossing queue/backpressure boundaries, making it impossible to connect high-level ingress spikes to downstream tail-latency and cache-eviction signals.

Impact: Investigators could not reliably identify which tenants or routes caused the ingress surge because request counts derived from application logs diverged from network-level traffic signals. This delayed mitigation, caused unnecessary capacity provisioning, and blocked effective post-incident frequency analysis.

Goal: Provide deterministic, low-overhead visibility from network ingress -> console request id -> runtime processing so on-call can: (a) quickly identify offending tenant/route, (b) see per-tenant tail-latency correlation, and (c) trigger targeted mitigations (rate-limit/fallback) without broad capacity changes.

Scope / Acceptance criteria: 
- Deploy eBPF-based per-edge-node metrics that export per-tenant ingress request counters and byte counts (tenant derived from host header / x-tenant / hashed identifier).
- Implement deterministic sampled-span policy at the ingress proxy so that one canonical span is always emitted for a small deterministic subset of requests (e.g., hashed sampling: 0.1% deterministic + upsampling to 100% for requests that later hit queue-length or 5xx thresholds).
- Add a new Console dashboard: "Ingress vs Request Lineage" showing ingress counters vs app-logged requests, ingress/request mismatch alert, and per-route tail-latency heatmap correlated to network spikes.
- Create runbook steps and an automated alert that runs the lightweight reconciliation job (ingress counters vs request IDs) and surface top-5 mismatched tenants.

Design decisions and trade-offs: 
- eBPF chosen to avoid instrumenting every proxy; we will extract minimal labels (tenant-hash, destination port, L7 path hash) to keep perf overhead low.
- Deterministic sampling reduces the need for pervasive full-trace capture while ensuring reproducible linkage between ingress and runtime traces. Upsampling rules will only apply when an anomaly threshold is triggered to bound storage/cost.
- Privacy: tenant-hash must be non-reversible; no PII will be exported. All telemetry flows through our existing metrics pipeline and is subject to KMS-encrypted storage policies.

Implementation notes: 
- Phase 1 (P1): prototype eBPF probe on staging edge pool, implement deterministic sampling in ingress proxy (staging flag), and add reconciliation dashboard.
- Phase 2 (P2): rollout to canary edge nodes, tune sampling ratio, add upsampling triggers tied to queue-depth and 5xx windows.
- Phase 3 (P3): full rollout, enable alerting, bake into post-incident runbook and on-call playbook.

Operational costs: Estimated additional metric cardinality ~ +10% for ingest; trace storage increase during anomalies only. We will set a 7-day high-fidelity retention window for sampled upsampled traces and a 30-day aggregated metric retention.

Documentation & artifacts: Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/ingress-request-lineage-eBPF-proposal, experimental design doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/obs/ingress-lineage-proto.md.

Risks: kernel compatibility across older edge kernels — we will use a userspace BPF loader with compatibility checks and fallback to a socket-mirror mode.

Next steps (short term): deploy probe to staging, open PR for deterministic sampler, create initial dashboard mockup and get PM/design review.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket after incident postmortem. Initial hypothesis attached to description and Confluence link.

2026-03-11 - Daniel Kim: Spun up a staging edge with eBPF probe; observed per-tenant counters with ~0.7% CPU overhead. Uploaded experimental results to Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/ingress-ebpf/staging-results.

2026-03-12 - Maria Gonzales (SRE): Verified deterministic sampler approach vs existing probabilistic sampling. Deterministic 0.1% produced stable linkage. Concern: during strong spikes upsampling will briefly increase trace volume; propose hard cap and adaptive windowing.
2026-03-13 - Security (R. Singh): Reviewed privacy implications — tenant-hash approach acceptable; require security review for any label changes. Marked security_review_required=true on ticket.

2026-03-14 - Daniel Kim: Opened PR for ingress proxy sampler: https://github.com/redwood/run-proxy/pull/2193. Created dashboard mock: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ingress-lineage/mock-20260314. Moving to canary once PR passes CI and perf tests.
2026-03-14 - Product (L. Ortega): Thumbs-up on alerting thresholds; requested add a "customer-visible impact" flag to the dashboard to quickly mark tenant incidents for CS escalation.
2026-03-14 - Aisha Patel: Added runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Ingress-Lineage-Runbook. Next on-call review scheduled 2026-03-18.
